item.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
item.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

item.title: Global finance ministers gather in North Carolina for G20 summit
item.description: The U.S. is playing host to finance ministers from around the world this week. Russia's top economic official made a stir on Monday when he showed up in person at the meeting in North Carolina.

item.title: The U.S. wants others to join its economic pressure campaign against Iran. Will they?
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks former Deputy National Security Adviser Jon Finer about U.S. efforts to cultivate global support to economically isolate and pressure Iran.

item.description: Among the hundreds still missing on Nepal's border with China are Hindus from India and beyond, participating in a journey of devotion to a sacred mountain.

item.title: Trump's plan for economic D-day for Iran has one big hole: China
item.description: The Trump administration says it's asking countries to voluntarily cut off business with Iran to squeeze its economy further. But the most critical country — China — already says it won't cooperate.

item.title: Lionel Messi says he's retiring from playing internationally for Argentina
item.description: The soccer star is ending 21 years of Argentine national-team duty but will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in U.S. Major League Soccer.

item.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths
item.description: The U.S. and Venezuela have entered into an oil deal. And, NPR spent two years tracking heat-related deaths and found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat more than the official counts show.

item.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
item.description: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.
